# Subsetting Astrocytes from All Celltype-Seurat

This is the first script of this project. In this project, I analysed single-nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNAseq) data of post-mortem spinal cord tissue of 20 ALS patients and 4 controls, focusing on astrocytes. In this script, I will open the full dataset (with all celltypes), examine the astrocytes (e.g. what proportion of total cells they form per sample), and subset the astrocytes.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-01-setup
#| include: false

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Helper functions

### theme_quarto() and theme_manuscript()

I created my own themes to add to figures. `theme_quarto()` is used to add themes to figures as displayed in the Quarto document and saved to disk as `.pdf` or `.png`. `theme_manuscript()` is used to add themes to figures as they will end up in the manuscript.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-06-helper-themes
theme_quarto <- function(
    legend_position = "right", 
    plot_title = element_blank()
    ) {
    theme(
      plot.title = plot_title,
      legend.position = legend_position
    )
}

theme_manuscript <- function(
    legend_position = "none",
    plot_title = element_blank(),
    axis_title_size = 8,
    axis_text_size = 6
    ) {
    theme(
      plot.title = plot_title,
      legend.position = legend_position,
      axis.title = element_text(size = axis_title_size),
      axis.text = element_text(size = axis_text_size),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"), 
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9)
    )
}

```

### save_plot()

This document displays all the figures I make, but I also want them saved to disk — both as `.png` and `.pdf`. I only need to provide the ggplot object, a filename (without extension), and optionally the width and height of the figure.

The figures for my written report contain subfigures spread across multiple scripts. Since I want to assemble these panel figures via R code rather than by hand, `save_plot()` can also optionally save the plot object itself to disk as an .rds file, for a final script to later combine with `patchwork`. Set figure to the name the figure should carry in the report (e.g. `"SF1A"`) to trigger this; leave it `NULL` (the default) to just save the `.png`/`.pdf` as normal.

A live ggplot object carries its underlying data along with it — for plots built from large Seurat objects, this can balloon the saved file to gigabytes. To avoid this, `save_plot()` converts the object to a grob (a static, pre-rendered drawing, with no data attached) before saving it as `.rds`. This is controlled by the `grob` argument, and defaults to `TRUE`, since converting a small plot costs nothing but forgetting to convert a large one is expensive. Set `grob = FALSE` only if a later step specifically needs the original, live ggplot object rather than its rendered form.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-05-helper-save-plot
save_plot <- function(
    p, filename, 
    width = 10, height = 6, 
    figure = NULL, grob = TRUE, apply_theme = TRUE, 
    add_tag = TRUE, tag_text_size = 14,
    legend_pos_manuscript = "none"
    ) {
  ## Save image on disk as png and pdf
  # Add Quarto-specific theme, unless the plot has its own custom theme
  if (apply_theme) {
    p_image <- p + theme_quarto()
  } else {
    p_image <- p
  }
  file_png <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  ggsave(file_png, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  file_pdf <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(file_pdf, p_image, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  
  ## Save the ggplot object on disk as an rds file 
  if (!is.null(figure)) {
    # Add tag if needed
    if (add_tag) {
      tag <- str_extract(figure, "[A-Z]$")
      p <- p + 
        labs(tag = tag) + 
        theme(
          plot.tag = element_text(
            face = "bold", 
            size = tag_text_size, 
            hjust = 0, vjust = 0
            )
        )
    }
    # Add manuscript-specific theme, unless the plot has its own custom theme
    if (apply_theme) {
      p <- p + theme_manuscript(legend_pos_manuscript)
    }
    file_rds <- file.path(dir_man, paste0(figure, ".rds"))
    # Convert the object to a grob if needed
    if (grob) {
      p <- ggplotGrob(p)
    }
    # Save on disk
    saveRDS(p, file_rds)
  }
}
```

### calc_freq()

In the section **Visualization Astrocyte Frequency**, I'll make barplots with the frequencies of cell types per sample. I will create figures which show the frequency of all cell types, but also one which just shows *astrocytes vs non-astrocytes*. To do this efficiently, I created the function calc_freq which can calculate both.


```{r}
#| label: chunk-07-helper-calc-freq
calc_freq <- function(metadata, col_celltype, col_sample = "AnonymousID") {
  freq_table <- table(
    metadata[, col_celltype],
    metadata[, col_sample]
  ) |>
    as.data.frame()
  colnames(freq_table) <- c("Celltype", "Sample", "Frequency")
  # Rearrange the columns so they are in a sensible order; as sample numbers are
  # given with single digits for single digit character, it's currently in the
  # order ALS1, ALS10, ALS11, ..., ALS19, ALS2, ALS20, ALS3, ALS4 etc. and does
  # not count up like we humans would.
  freq_table <- freq_table |>
    mutate(
      Sample = fct_relevel(
        Sample, str_sort(unique(as.character(Sample)), numeric = TRUE)
      )
    )
  freq_table
}
```

### bar_freq()

`bar_freq()` creates the visualizations of the same section. The argument freq_type becomes the argument to position in geom_bar: "stack" makes it absolute, "fill" makes it proportional. I added the argument `just_astro` because I want to manually colour the plot red vs grey in case of the astrocyte vs non-astrocyte plot. The function assumes you provide the output of `calc_freq()` as input. I added the argument `theme_manuscript` because I wanted to apply the functions `theme_quarto()` and `theme_manuscript()`, but applying these themes after I ran the function `bar_freq()` meant that ` + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))` gets overwritten - which is essential for making the x-axis readable. Thus, I had to add `theme_quarto()` or `theme_manuscript()` within the `bar_freq()` function, so I can adjust x-axis labels afterwards.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-08-helper-bar-freq
# The argument freq_type becomes the argument to position in geom_bar.
# "stack" makes it absolute, "fill" makes it proportional.
bar_freq <- function(freq_table, freq_type = "fill", just_astro = FALSE,
                    theme_manuscript = FALSE) {
  p_bar <- ggplot(freq_table, aes(fill = Celltype, y = Frequency, x = Sample)) +
    geom_bar(position = freq_type, stat = "identity")

  # Rotate x-axis labels, otherwise the x-axis becomes unreadable 
  p_bar <- p_bar + 
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) 

  if (just_astro) {
    p_bar <- p_bar + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EF2400", "grey"))
  }

  p_bar
}
```

# Astrocytes in the dataset with all celltypes

## Load Seurat in from disk

The object `seu_spinal_allcelltypes_shortread_postQC.rds` was the object which \[name\] shared with me after her full QC.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-09-open-seurat
file_rds <- file.path(dir_data_in, "seu_shortread_allcelltypes_postQC.rds")
seu <- readRDS(file_rds)
# Test whether it loaded in correctly
seu
```
The metadata can be structured a little better, so I'll do that now, and then it's changed for the rest of the scripts.

Some ugliness in the metadata, I'm fixing it here, in the root.
- In the column pTDP-43 stage, all controls and samples ALS17 and ALS18 are empty. For the controls, that's because they do not have ALS and no pTDP-43 pathology, but samples ALS17 and ALS 18 are empty because they have FUS ALS - which has a different pathology.
- Only one sample has pTDP-43 stage 2, so I lumped it together with 3 - otherwise comparison with stage 2 always looks weird, because it has n = 1.
- The controls have empty strings in the column `primary_site_of_onset`, set these to `"Ctrl"`.
- There was not yet a column with `ALS` vs `Ctrl`, so I added the column `condition`.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-10-fix-metadata
metadata <- seu@meta.data

# How to fix the metadata of pTDP-43 stage and other columns
metadata <- metadata |>
  mutate(
    condition = ifelse(
      str_detect(AnonymousID, "Ctrl") == TRUE,
      "Ctrl",
      "ALS"
    ),
    pTDP.43.Stage = case_when(
      AnonymousID %in% c("ALS17", "ALS18") ~ "FUS ALS",
      str_detect(AnonymousID, "Ctrl") == TRUE ~ "Ctrl",
      .default = as.character(pTDP.43.Stage)
    ),
    # The Ctrls have "" at primary_site_of_onset. Make this "Ctrl"
    primary_site_of_onset = ifelse(
      str_detect(AnonymousID, "Ctrl") == TRUE,
      "Ctrl",
      primary_site_of_onset
    ),
    pTDP43_lumped = case_when(
      pTDP.43.Stage %in% c("2", "3") ~ "2 & 3",
      .default = as.character(pTDP.43.Stage)
    ),
    # This relevel steps makes the visualizations make more sense
    pTDP43_lumped = fct_relevel(pTDP43_lumped, "Ctrl", "FUS ALS")
  )
# Still need to order factor levels?

seu@meta.data <- metadata
```

## Visualization annotation all celltypes

\[name\] defined major cell types using a publicly available atlas of the human spinal cord of the Allan Brain Insitute. These are stored in the columns `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass` and `predicted.id_coarse_allen_group`, with the latter having a more subdivided annotation than the former.

```{r}
#| label: fig-01-umap-subclass
#| fig-cap: "UMAP of all cell types, coloured by Allen subclass annotation"
# I want to show both subclass and cellclass. First show subclass
p_allen_subclass <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE,
  label.size = 2,
  raster = TRUE
  ) + 
  labs(x = "UMAP1", y = "UMAP2")
p_allen_subclass + theme_quarto(legend_position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-02-umap-cellclass
#| fig-cap: "UMAP of all cell types, coloured by Allen cellclass annotation"
p_allen_group <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_group",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE
)
p_allen_group + theme_quarto(legend_position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-10-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plots, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_allen_subclass, "allcelltypes_umap_alansubclass", figure = "F3A")
save_plot(p_allen_group, "allcelltypes_umap_alangroup")
```


## Visualization astrocyte markers

I previously provided the annotation of celltypes, but I would like to confirm that the labelled astrocytes are astrocytes. A FeaturePlot() with astrocyte-marker genes forms a quick way to do so. In the default settings of this document, I provided the astrocyte marker genes `c("GFAP", "AQP4", "SLC1A2", "OBI1-AS1")`. You can see that the astrocyte cluster expresses these markers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-03-featureplot
#| fig-cap: "Featureplot of astrocyte markers"
p_feature <- FeaturePlot(
  seu,
  features = astro_markers,
  reduction = "umap"
)
p_feature + theme_quarto()
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-11-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_feature, "allcelltypes_featureplot")
```

## Visualization astrocyte frequency

I want to show how many astrocytes each sample has. I will create multiple types of barplots.
- visualizations of proportional frequency and visualizations with relative frequency (as scRNAseq data is proportional)
- visualizations with the frequency of all celltypes vs visualizations with just astrocytes vs non-astrocytes

This section uses the functions `calc_freq` and `bar_freq`, which I created myself in the section **Helper functions**.

### Frequency of all cell types

I will visualize using the column `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass`, which is the same one as used in the first image under the header **Visualization annotation all celltypes**.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-12-preprocessing-freq
# Extract dataframe from seurat object
metadata <- seu@meta.data |>
  as.data.frame()
# Calculate frequencies of celltypes
freq_table <- calc_freq(
  metadata,
  "predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass",
  "AnonymousID"
)

# Show the top rows in the knitted file
kable(head(freq_table))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-04-absolute-freq
#| fig-cap: "Absolute frequency of cell types"
p_abs <- bar_freq(freq_table, "stack")
p_abs + theme_quarto()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-05-proportional-freq
#| fig-cap: "Proportional frequency of cell types"
#| # This ones a little fancier atm because it's in the manuscript
p_prop <- bar_freq(freq_table, "fill") +
  labs(y = "Proportion") +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_blank()
    )
p_prop + theme_quarto()
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-13-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_abs, "allcelltypes_barplot_abs")

# For 4B, I need to adjust the legend a little, so I will run theme_manuscript
# manually so I can adjust legendsize afterwards
p_prop <- p_prop  + theme_manuscript(legend_position = "right") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1))  +
  theme(
    legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"), 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
    legend.title = element_blank()
    )
save_plot(p_prop, "allcelltypes_barplot_prop", figure = "F3B", 
          apply_theme = FALSE)
```


### Frequency astrocyte vs non-astrocyte

```{r}
#| label: chunk-14-preprocessing-freq
# Make a column which states whether something is an astrocyte or not
metadata$astro <- ifelse(
  test = metadata$predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes",
  yes = "Astrocyte",
  no = "Non-Astrocyte"
)

# Calculate frequencies of astrocyte vs non-astrocyte per sample
freq_table <- calc_freq(metadata, "astro", "AnonymousID")

# Show the top rows in the knitted file
kable(head(freq_table))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-06-absolute-freq
#| fig-cap: "Absolute frequency of astrocyte vs non-astrocyte"
p_abs <- bar_freq(freq_table, "stack", just_astro = TRUE)
p_abs
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-07-proportional-freq
#| fig-cap: "Proportional frequency of astrocyte vs non-astrocyte"
p_prop <- bar_freq(freq_table, "fill", just_astro = TRUE)
p_prop
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-15-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_abs, "allcelltypes_barplot_abs_just_astro")
save_plot(p_prop, "allcelltypes_barplot_prop_just_astro")
```

# Subset astrocytes and save on disk

Now that we have inspected the astrocytes in the whole dataset, I can subset the astrocytes which I will continue in the rest of the project. I wil subset the astrocytes as annotated in the column `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass`, which was visualized in @fig-01-umap-subclass.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-16-subset-astros
seu_astros <- subset(
  seu,
  subset = predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes"
)
# Inspect
seu_astros
```

Even though one could technically still call this a raw file (I have not done any preprocessing besides subsetting the astrocytes), I will store it in the folder `data/processed` rather than `data/raw`: I count the subsetting as preprocessing.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-17-save-to-disk
file_rds <- file.path(dir_data_out, "seu_shortread_astros_subset.rds")
saveRDS(seu_astros, file_rds)
```
